results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache | alphaXiv
results.content:
Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant memory challenges during inference, particularly from the Key-Value (KV) cache that stores intermediate attention states. This cache prevents redundant computation during auto-regressive text generation but can consume terabytes of memory for large batch sizes and long contexts, often exceeding the model parameters themselves. The KV cache creates a bottleneck that limits inference throughput and increases serving costs. [...] This paper is cited as a key related work that also tackles the KV cache bottleneck. KIVI's authors reference FlexGen's use of 4-bit group-wise quantization for both key and value caches, positioning their own asymmetric quantization strategy as a more nuanced and effective approach for lower bit-rates. [...] Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, Ying Sheng, Lianmin Zheng, Cody Hao Yu, Joseph Gonzalez, Hao Zhang, and Ion Stoica. Efficient memory management for large language model serving with pagedattention. In Proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, pages 611–626, 2023.

# Title:KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache

Authors:Zirui Liu, Jiayi Yuan, Hongye Jin, Shaochen Zhong, Zhaozhuo Xu, Vladimir Braverman, Beidi Chen, Xia Hu [...] > Abstract:Efficiently serving large language models (LLMs) requires batching of many requests to reduce the cost per request. Yet, with larger batch sizes and longer context lengths, the key-value (KV) cache, which stores attention keys and values to avoid re-computations, significantly increases memory demands and becomes the new bottleneck in speed and memory usage. Additionally, the loading of the KV cache causes the computational core to be idle, which limits the inference speed. results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
results.content:
Pairs with PagedAttention: KIVI reduces per-block memory, PagedAttention reduces fragmentation, both are needed for production LLM serving
 In system design: cite when asked about serving LLMs at scale, long-context support, or reducing per-request memory cost [...] Why KV cache is the bottleneck: for a 7B model serving 4K context at batch 32, KV cache alone is ~16GB (larger than model weights in INT4)
 Asymmetric insight: K has per-channel outliers → quantize per-channel; V has per-token outliers → quantize per-token. Getting this backwards destroys quality.
 Residual tokens: keep recent ~128 tokens in full precision, attention to recent context is more sensitive to quantization noise [...] Production-ready: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and other serving frameworks have adopted KV cache quantization inspired by this work
 Practical impact: Directly increases the max batch size and sequence length you can serve on a given GPU

results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache — Lacuna
results.content:
## Limitations and Future Work

While KIVI is highly effective, the authors note a few areas for improvement: [...] When serving LLMs, the "KV cache" is a major headache. To avoid re-calculating attention for every new word, models store the "Keys" and "Values" of previous tokens in memory. As batch sizes grow and context windows lengthen (e.g., a chatbot remembering a whole book), this cache balloons in size. [...] 1. Memory Capacity: Servers run out of VRAM, limiting how many users can be served concurrently.
2. Memory Bandwidth: The GPU spends more time moving this massive cache from main memory to its internal processors than it does actually performing calculations.

While quantizing model weights is common, quantizing the KV cache to ultra-low precision (like 2-bit) usually destroys model accuracy.

results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache [Quick Review]
results.content:
Efficiently serving large language models necessitates batching many requests, yet increased batch sizes and context lengths make KV cache a significant memory and speed bottleneck.
 Quantization can reduce KV cache size, but a lack of in-depth studies exists on its element distribution, hindering effective quantization strategies.
 This research aims to analyze KV cache element distribution in LLMs to identify optimal quantization approaches and overcome current limitations. [...] + For challenging tasks like GSM8K, KIVI's ability to maintain a small, full-precision sliding window for the most recent key and value tokens is crucial. While a naive 2-bit (K per-channel, V per-token) fake quantization shows significant accuracy drops on GSM8K (e.g., 13.50 to 5.76 for Llama-2-7B), KIVI-2, by incorporating this full-precision window, largely mitigates this degradation (e.g., 13.50 to 12.74 for Llama-2-7B), highlighting the importance of preserving local context in [...] 0
